name: Extreme heat – southern BC (2021 heat dome)

geo.extent: Southern British Columbia, including the normally mild coast

description: The June 2021 heat dome set a Canadian record of 49.6 °C at Lytton on 29 June. The BC Coroners Service identified 619 heat-related deaths (25 June–1 July 2021); 98% occurred indoors, 67% of those who died were 70 or older and 56% lived alone; 74% were in the Fraser and Vancouver Coastal health regions.

documented_events: June 2021: Lytton 49.6 °C; 619 heat-related deaths in BC (BC Coroners Service; ECCC 2021)
practical_implications: Homes on the coast are often built without air conditioning
Check cooling in rentals; vulnerable people living alone
Extreme hot temperatures will become more frequent and more intense (CCCR 2019)

sources.title: Extreme Heat and Human Mortality: A Review of Heat-Related Deaths in B.C. in Summer 2021 (BC Coroners Service death review panel, 2022)
sources.publisher: Government of British Columbia – BC Coroners Service

sources.title: Canada's Changing Climate Report (2019) – Headline statements
sources.publisher: Government of Canada (Environment and Climate Change Canada, lead)
sources.methodology: Assessment report; statements are assessments of observed and projected change, not local forecasts

verification.notes: Event facts quoted or paraphrased from the cited official pages on 2026-10-30. Exposure and implications are agent-04 interpretation.

limitations: Heat-day counts per station are in the clim records (days with maximum > 30 °C, humidex ≥ 30). Past events show exposure; they are not a prediction for any particular year. Exposure varies street by street – check municipal and provincial hazard maps for a specific property.
